note: Models this application can actually run, with the preprocessing and decoding it relies on. There is deliberately no 'load any ONNX model' option: supporting an arbitrary artifact would mean guessing its input layout, normalisation and output decoding, and guessing those produces confident numbers that mean nothing.

models.runtime: @tensorflow/tfjs 4.x, WebGL backend with a CPU fallback
models.artifactHashNote: Served by a third-party CDN. No checksum is published here because none was independently verified; recording an unchecked hash would be worse than recording none.
models.downloadNote: Measured by summing model.json and the Content-Length of all 5 weight shards.
models.inputResolution: native image size; the graph resizes internally to 300x300
models.normalization: uint8 [0,255] input; normalisation is baked into the graph
models.resizeBehavior: bilinear resize inside the SavedModel graph, aspect ratio not preserved
models.outputLayout: boxes in pixel coordinates [x, y, width, height] plus class label and score
models.classMapping: COCO 80 classes, mapped to label strings by the coco-ssd package
models.nmsBehavior: non-max suppression applied by the coco-ssd package
models.roleNote: A practical baseline detector. Not a representative sample of current detectors, and results do not transfer to other models.

notSupported.reason: Not shipped. Adding a second inference runtime is only worth its bundle cost once there is a verified artifact behind it: licence, input layout, normalisation, resize behaviour and a tested output decoder. src/features/evaluation/adapter.ts is the seam it would use.
